about.p1: I'm David Somadina Obichukwu, known online as xTc. I build products from end to end: I find the idea, design how it should feel, and build it until it works.
about.p2b: My route into building started on the practical side of technology. Installing systems, deploying products and supporting customers at Smile Tech taught me to start from the person using the product, and to make things that keep working when nobody is watching. Today I also evaluate AI output as an AI Data Annotation Specialist at Elevate Labs.
about.p3b: I work across software, product design and games. I can read, write and debug code on my own, and I use AI coding assistants as tools, not as a replacement for understanding what ships. Toilet Wars, PitchIT, EchoMind and the client sites are very different products, but they come from the same habit: take an idea seriously enough to finish it.

ai-land.fact0: AI and real estate technology, product concept
ai-land.heroAlt: Concept artwork: an isometric land plot with roads and buildings, a new structure being placed, a tools panel and scenario comparisons
ai-land.lede: A product concept for AI assisted land planning. Users would work with a virtual model of a piece of land, add, remove and reposition structures, and compare different development scenarios before anything is built. Nothing has been implemented yet; this is a concept I am learning toward.

s0.p0: Plans on paper and static drawings are hard to imagine, and changing them is slow and expensive. Owners and small developers often decide what to build on a plot without seeing the alternatives side by side.

s1.p0: Put the land into an interactive 3D environment where ideas can be tried directly: place a structure, move it, remove it, and see the result immediately. Save each arrangement as a scenario and compare them.

s2.i0: Land owners deciding what to do with a plot

s3.d0: Start from the plot's shape and size.
s3.d1: Drop in buildings, roads and green space from a library.
s3.d2: Move, rotate and remove elements, and see the layout change in 3D.
s3.d3: Save alternatives and compare them side by side.

f0.d: A navigable model of the plot.

f3.d: Clear views of what each scenario would look like.

s4.note: None of these exist yet. They describe the concept.

s5.i0: Suggesting layouts that fit the plot
s5.i1: Checking a layout against simple rules such as access and spacing

s6.p0: I am learning the 3D and simulation side needed to prototype this, starting with interactive environments, which I already work with in Roblox Studio.

s7.i0: Cost and material estimates per scenario
s7.i2: Use for estates and community planning

s8.p0: The image at the top is concept artwork. There is no working platform or AI planning engine.

ai-studio.fact3: Creative direction, product design and development
ai-studio.heroAlt: Concept artwork of the studio: a footage bin, a cinematic preview, creative direction and style options, detected moments and a timeline synced to the beat
ai-studio.lede: A personal AI powered creative studio that brings video editing, photo editing and audio work into one place. I give it footage and a creative direction, and it makes editing decisions with an understanding of what happens in the clip. Today an experimental Python and FFmpeg engine exists; the studio around it is still the plan.

s0.p0: I want edits with taste and intention, from gaming montages and football highlights to cinematic, vlog, travel and promo cuts, without cutting every frame by hand and without depending on expensive AI subscriptions.

f0.d: A Python and FFmpeg pipeline that cuts, sequences and renders clips automatically.

f1.d: Cuts that follow what actually happens, such as a kill or a goal, instead of random cuts.

f2.d: Gaming montages, cinematic, vlog, promo, travel and football highlight edits.

f3.d: Transitions and effects only where they help, with cuts placed on the beat of the music.

f4.d: Audio placement, voiceover integration, and original audio kept by default.

f5.d: Photo edits in the same studio and the same visual styles.

f6.d: A visual studio on top of the engine, deliberately left until the engine is right.

s1.note: Built means it runs today in the experimental engine. Everything else is the direction of the product.

s2.i0: Local first: it has to run on an everyday laptop
s2.i1: Outside AI only where it truly helps
s2.i2: Original audio stays unless I say otherwise
s2.i3: Built for my own creative work first

s3.p0: The first real test, a 30 second gaming clip with two kills, produced random cuts, effects that were not needed and missing original audio. That result set the direction: the studio has to understand events before it decides where to cut, and the original sound stays by default.

s5.p0: The image at the top is concept artwork of the intended studio. No interface has been built yet.

ai-studio.tagline: Footage in, a considered edit out.

bookverse.fact3: Product owner, design direction and development
bookverse.heroAlt: BookVerse home page: Editor's pick, Frankenstein by Mary Shelley, free to read, with Read free online and Download free buttons
bookverse.lede: BookVerse is a digital book platform for readers who move between formats: novels, manga, manhwa, manhua, webtoons, comics, graphic novels, web and light novels, audiobooks, poetry and non fiction. A first release is live as a preview. The reader, the full catalogue, Top Books and the writer studio are still being built.

s0.p0: Readers no longer stay in one format. The same person reads a classic novel, follows a webtoon and listens to an audiobook, but each lives on a different site with its own account and its own way of keeping a library. Writers face the same split when they want to publish.

s1.p0: One structured place to discover books, keep a personal library and, later, write and publish next to the classics. Discovery is organised by format and genre, every book is honestly labelled with where it can be read, and readership numbers will only ever come from real readers.

s2.d0: Browse by format, genre or author, or search, and open a book page that says plainly what you can read here, borrow or buy elsewhere.
s2.d1: Read free editions on BookVerse itself with reading settings for text, comics and audio.
s2.d2: Save books to a personal library and organise it.
s2.d3: Writers publish books, serials, poetry and comics from one author profile, with a name and handle that are theirs.

f1.d: Fiction and non fiction genres with short descriptions and sub genres such as epic fantasy, dystopian, crime and gothic.

f2.d: Public domain books list where to read or download them free, from sources such as Standard Ebooks and Project Gutenberg.

f3.d: Eight colour themes, accent colours and separate settings for text, comics and audio, with accessible reading fonts.

personal-ai.lede: A personal AI system that acts as one central intelligence: coder, designer, researcher and email and productivity assistant, with its own animated desktop interface and voice, and later a mobile companion. It runs on my own laptop first and is built so that I stay in control of what it learns and what it can do.

s0.p0: Paid AI subscriptions add up, and each tool knows only a slice of my work. I want one system that knows my projects, runs locally where it can, and is not tied to a single provider.

s1.i2: Learns only from sources I explicitly authorise
s1.i3: Every memory can be inspected, edited and deleted, and follows my approval rules
s1.i4: It can never expand its own permissions

s2.i3: Handle email and day to day productivity
s2.i4: Talk by voice through its own animated desktop interface
s2.i6: Host the xTc Personal AI Studio for photo and video editing

s0.p0: Tycoon games are about growth: start small, build up, unlock more. Steal the Moon gives that growth a goal worth chasing and adds risk: what you collect can be stolen, so you have to defend as well as build.

s1.d0: Each player claims a base of their own when they join.
s1.d1: Gather resources around the world and from your base to power the economy.
s1.d2: Spend what you collect on upgrades that make your base produce and protect more.
s1.d3: Protect your base from other players, or travel to theirs and take what you can.
s1.d4: Daily rewards and long term goals bring players back to repeat the loop.

s2.i0: Claimable player bases and base ownership
s2.i5: A daily spin, a rarity mixer, the Moonlog and upgrades

s3.p0: Robux products have to be things players genuinely want. No pay to win, no fake scarcity and no pressure tactics, and existing player data and balances are always preserved through updates.

toilet-wars.fact2: 1v1 up to 4v4, bots fill empty slots
toilet-wars.fact3: Concept, game direction, design and development
toilet-wars.heroAlt: Toilet Wars gameplay scene: a player with a golden plunger knocks a soaked rival at 187 percent toward the bowl, under the Plunger Brawler title
toilet-wars.lede: Toilet Wars is a team based multiplayer arena game on Roblox. Two teams, the Red Plungers and the Blue Scrubbers, soak each other with plungers, toilet paper launchers and flush bombs, then knock their rivals off the map. It is public on Roblox and I keep developing it.

s0.p0: Roblox is a platform where millions of people play games made by independent creators, on phones, computers, tablets and consoles. Toilet Wars is one of those games, and anyone can join it from the Roblox app or website.
s0.p1: It is a knockback brawler: instead of losing health, players get soaked, and the aim is to send rivals flying off the arena or into the bowl. Matches are short, loud and team based, built for playing with friends.

s1.d0: Press Play, choose a map and a team size from 1v1 to 4v4. Bots fill any empty slots so a match can always start.
s1.d1: Every hit with a plunger, a toilet paper roll or a flush bomb raises a rival's soak percentage, shown above their head.
s1.d2: Soaked players are easier to send flying. Push them off the map or into the bowl, while your team holds the objective.
s1.d3: Build up your Super Flush and release it for a blast that can turn a round.
s1.d4: Rounds feed daily rewards, quests, challenges and the Flush Pass, which unlock cosmetics.

s10.p0: Public on Roblox since November 2026 and actively developed: new balance passes, content and fixes follow play testing.

s2.i3: A Practice Range for new players

s3.i0: Plunger weapons for close range hits
s3.i3: Super Flush, a charged special ability

s6.i0: Free daily rewards and login streaks
s6.i1: Daily quests, weekly challenges and achievements
s6.i2: Season 1 Flush Pass with 15 tiers of rewards
s6.i3: A daily featured shop with skins, hats, trails, titles, emotes and victory animations
s6.i5: Parties so friends can play together

s7.d0: The idea, the tone and the rules are mine: a silly theme with a competitive core, readable for younger players and deep enough to keep playing.
s7.d1: I planned the soak and knockback rules, the three modes, the chaos events, team sizes from 1v1 to 4v4 and how rewards should feel fair.
s7.d2: The game is scripted in Luau. I write and change code myself and use an AI coding assistant heavily to draft systems, debug and review, then I read, adjust and decide what ships.
s7.d3: Five obstacle course maps, a lobby with map and team size selection, and a HUD that shows soak percentages clearly on phones and computers.
s7.d4: Play sessions in Studio and on Roblox after each change, then balance passes on knockback, events and rewards.

f.aiD: Optional AI features that help you spot patterns in your entries. You choose to turn them on, and the private core keeps working without them.
f.checkinD: Choose every feeling that fits, rate how strong it is and add a short note about what's behind it. If you can't name it yet, choose "I'm not sure yet".
f.insightsD: The last 7 or 30 days at a glance: how often you checked in, how many days you noted something, your daily rhythm and the feelings you named most. Patterns only appear once there is enough to show.
f.journeyD: Everything you noted on one timeline, as it happened, with search and filters for feelings, writing and saved moments.
f.mindD: Bookmark the moments you want to keep and find them together in one place.
f.ownD: Create a feeling with your own name, emoji and colour, and mark it as pleasant, difficult or mixed. Any feeling can be renamed, recoloured or hidden.
f.privateD: Everything is stored only on your phone, in EchoMind's private storage. There is no account and no internet connection, and your writing is never sent anywhere.
f.storeD: Moving from the shared test build to a store release.
f.themeD: Deep evening tones, warm light paper, or match your phone. A Reduce motion switch is built in, and your phone's own setting is respected too.
f.voiceD2: Record up to 30 minutes with pause and resume, then listen back, add a title, note or feeling, and save or discard it. Interrupted recordings are recovered, and audio never leaves the phone.
f.writeD: Write freely, or start from a daily prompt such as "What happened today?".

p.apkNote: The test build is an Android APK shared through Google Drive. It is not on Google Play yet, so Android may ask you to allow installs from this source.
p.audience1: People who want a private, easy way to reflect: students, busy professionals, and anyone who wants to see how their days really feel over time.
p.audience2: EchoMind is a tool for reflecting on your own feelings. It is not a medical, diagnostic or therapy service.
p.lede: EchoMind is a journaling and mood app for Android. Check in with how you feel, write freely or from a daily prompt, and look back on everything in your Journey. All of it stays on your phone. There is no account, no subscription and no internet connection.
p.problem1: Many people want to understand their moods but don't keep up with journaling. Writing takes effort, and most journaling apps want an account and keep your most personal thoughts in someone else's cloud.
p.problem2: EchoMind lowers both barriers. Checking in takes a few taps, a daily prompt gives you somewhere to start, and nothing you record ever leaves your phone.
p.shotsNote: Screenshots from the current Android build in the Dusk theme. Select one to view it full size.

echomind.s3D: Soft colour bubbles, a deep evening palette and gentle motion, with plain words throughout and a switch for anyone who wants less animation.
echomind.s4D: Built in Flutter and tested on a physical Android phone throughout, so it works well on everyday devices.
echomind.s4T: Build and test on real hardware
echomind.s5D: AI features are planned as an optional layer, so the journal stays useful and private even without them.
echomind.s5T: Add AI on top, never underneath
echomind.summary: Check in with every feeling that fits, write about your day and look back on your Journey. Everything stays on your phone, with no account and no internet connection.

f.atmoD: Each house has its own look, from the farmhouse's worn timber to the Mother's red bedroom, lit by lanterns and candles.
f.coopD: Multiplayer rounds with private answers, so nobody can copy and every player is tested.
f.mobileD: Large touch controls and a clear HUD make it playable on mobile as well as desktop.
f.puzzleD: Players study a room, then have to notice what's different. Easy to learn, tense to master.
f.surviveD: A countdown, a candle meter and limited power ups such as Revive, Rewind and Tracker make every guess count.

p.b1: Multiplayer rounds where each player locks in a private answer
p.b2: Three house environments, with doors and interactive objects to search
p.b3: Hunter behaviour that adds pressure while players explore
p.b4: Lobby management and match progression from house to house
p.b5: Gameplay variations so changes differ between runs
p.b6: A player interface built for touch: timers, candle meter, power ups and the shop
p.b7: Iterative testing and fixes after each play session
p.builtLede: I designed the game and built it in Roblox Studio with Luau, writing and changing scripts myself and using an AI coding assistant to draft and debug, then testing every round in play sessions.
p.capNote: Captured inside the game on a phone. Select a shot to view it full size.
p.game1: Every house plays out in three phases. Explore it and pick up what you find. Memorize a room before the timer runs out. Then come back, tap whatever changed, and lock in your answer.
p.game2: In multiplayer, each player locks in a private answer, so everyone has to trust their own memory. A candle meter, power ups and a shop inside the game add pressure and strategy to each run.
p.lede: Haunting Mother is a multiplayer horror puzzle game on Roblox. Players explore three haunted houses, memorize each room against the clock, then have to spot what changed. Best played with friends, in the dark, with the sound up.
p.playNote: Opens the experience on Roblox. You'll need a free Roblox account to play.

phase.changedD: Tap the difference, then lock in your answer.

phase.memorizeD: Study the room while the countdown runs.

haunting.s1D: Designed the loop of exploring, memorizing and spotting the change, the three houses and how difficulty builds from one to the next.
haunting.s2D: Built and furnished each house and tuned its lighting for atmosphere.
haunting.s3D: Scripted the phases, timers, answer checking, items and multiplayer behaviour in Luau, Roblox's scripting language.
haunting.s4D: Playtested in Studio and published the game as a public Roblox experience.
haunting.s5D: Designed the HUD: the phase card with timer and candles, item slots, the objective panel, the private answer panel and touch controls.
haunting.summary: Three haunted houses, timed memory rounds, power ups and a HUD built for touch. Designed, scripted and published in Roblox Studio.
haunting.tagline: A multiplayer horror memory game. Study every room, then spot what changed.

f.adminD: Users, jobs, disputes, categories and review moderation, with every admin action recorded.
f.chatD: One conversation per job and worker, with photos, read receipts and notifications.
f.findD: Search, filters for category, budget, remote work and distance, and a Nearby map with price pins.
f.locD: GPS, a pin on the map or a typed place, with the main landmark, street or junction, building, written directions and reference photos.
f.offerD: Workers offer a price, availability and experience. Customers compare offers by recommended, lowest price or top rated, and team slots can never overfill.
f.payD: A clearly labelled simulated mode, plus Paystack test and live modes verified on the server.
f.postD: 13 sectors and 105 subcategories, plus your own category. Nine work arrangements, from one time and hourly to seasonal and emergency, and team jobs with several workers.
f.privD: Before funding, workers only see an approximate area. The exact pin unlocks for the hired worker after funding, and the database enforces it.
f.respD: A bottom bar on phones, a side rail on tablets and desktops, and two pane layouts for jobs and messages.
f.trustD: Reviews only after completion, phone and ID verification badges, reports, and disputes with evidence, an admin decision and one appeal.

p.demoNote: The demo is the real app running in demo mode: sample data held in your browser and clearly labelled simulated payments. No account is needed and nothing is sent to a server.
p.design1: Warm, confident and plain spoken. A bright orange on soft cream, rounded Plus Jakarta Sans type and large touch targets, so the app feels friendly on a cheap phone in bright sunlight.
p.design2: The words matter as much as the visuals. Screens say Find work and Hire someone, not marketplace jargon, and every money step says clearly when a payment is simulated.
p.featNote: Everything listed here is built and can be tried in the demo, except live payments, which need a real backend.
p.journeysD: The same account can hire and work. A Hiring and Working switch changes the whole navigation to fit the role.
p.lede: PitchIT is a marketplace for every kind of work in Nigeria: farm hands, fish traders, market help, artisans, movers, cleaners, errands and professionals. People who need work done post a job. People who can do it send offers. The customer funds the agreed amount before the work starts.
p.opp1: Most work in Nigeria never appears on a job board. It happens through word of mouth, at the market, on the farm and by the roadside.
p.opp2: That shaped the product. Nobody needs a CV to sign up. Locations are described the way people actually give directions, by landmark, junction and building. And the app has to stay light enough for everyday phones and patchy connections.
p.platform: Android and web, with layouts for phone, tablet and desktop
p.shotsNote: Screenshots from the Android build. Select one to view it full size.

p.status2: The next steps are connecting the production backend, live payments and a first group of real customers and workers.

pitchit.s1D: Started from how work is found and described in Nigeria, which led to the sector list, landmark directions and the no CV sign up.
pitchit.s2D: Privacy, slot limits and funding are enforced by Postgres row level security, not just hidden in the interface.
pitchit.s3D: More than 50 security and workflow checks on a real Postgres 16 database, plus unit and widget tests for sign in, posting, offers, hiring and funding.
pitchit.s4D: Continuous integration analyses the code, runs the tests, takes screenshots at four sizes and builds the web app and the Android APK.
pitchit.s5D: Without backend keys the app runs in demo mode, which is the version embedded on this page.
pitchit.summary: A marketplace that connects people who need work done with the people who do it, across 13 sectors, from farming and fishing to trades, errands and professional services. It is built for how work really happens in Nigeria: directions from landmarks instead of street addresses, and jobs funded before the work begins.
pitchit.w4: Finish, get paid and build a reputation
